document_purpose: Contexto de consenso pré-call para ferramenta de análise de earnings calls. Usar como base externa para detectar surpresa, calibrar score e limitar inferências.

hierarchy: 1. Consenso formal Bloomberg/LSEG quando citado por veículos confiáveis.
2. Prévia sell-side pública de casa de research quando disponível diretamente.
3. Prévia sell-side via veículos financeiros quando relatório original é fechado.
4. Relatórios pós-resultado apenas para validar actuals, guidance e leitura de surpresa, não como contexto pré-call puro.
limitations: Bloomberg Terminal, LSEG Workspace, FactSet, S&P Capital IQ e Visible Alpha não foram acessados diretamente; apenas referências públicas ao consenso Bloomberg/LSEG foram utilizadas.
Algumas estimativas de casas como Itaú BBA, BTG, BBI e Goldman vieram de veículos que resumiram relatórios proprietários; por isso recebem confiança média.
O campo post_result_actuals deve ser usado apenas para backtesting e avaliação de surpresa, não como informação disponível antes da call.
Métricas podem ter definições diferentes entre casas; por exemplo, despesas administrativas podem incluir ou excluir pessoal/linhas específicas.
Post-result actuals and post-result sell-side commentary are explicitly labeled and must not be treated as pre-call expectations.

S11_Reuters_prior_guidance.allowed_usage: Prior formal 2026 guidance and LSEG reference before 1Q26; use as pre-call context.

known_before_call: Asset-quality pressure in agribusiness was already expected and was the central pre-call risk theme.
Adjusted net income around R$3.5bn was expected by Bloomberg/LSEG and public sell-side previews.
ROE below 10% was expected; Genial estimated 7.3% and Itaú BBA 7.5%.
High provisions/cost of credit were expected; Genial estimated R$17.9bn for 1Q26.
A risk of negative 2026 guidance revision was already known, especially in cost of credit and adjusted net income.
NII resilience was partly expected, although sequential pressure from seasonality/funding/treasury was also part of the narrative.
The first half of 2026 was expected to remain weak, with any recovery more likely concentrated in 2H26.
unknown_before_call: Exact magnitude of the cost-of-credit guidance revision.
Whether the new cost-of-credit guidance would exceed R$60bn by a large margin.
Whether management would signal credit pressure beyond agribusiness, especially in individuals, credit card and revolving lines.
Whether capital/CET1 and dividend capacity would become a central topic rather than a secondary risk.
Whether management would provide credible visibility on normalization in 2H26 or keep visibility low.
Whether the guidance revision would be framed as conservative/final or as potentially still exposed to further downside.
Whether NII would offset credit pressure enough to support earnings quality.
potential_surprises_before_call: Exact magnitude of the cost-of-credit guidance revision.
Whether the new cost-of-credit guidance would exceed R$60bn by a large margin.
Whether management would signal credit pressure beyond agribusiness, especially in individuals, credit card and revolving lines.
Whether capital/CET1 and dividend capacity would become a central topic rather than a secondary risk.
Whether management would provide credible visibility on normalization in 2H26 or keep visibility low.
Whether the guidance revision would be framed as conservative/final or as potentially still exposed to further downside.
Whether NII would offset credit pressure enough to support earnings quality.

new_guidance_after_result.usage_warning: This is a post-result fact. It must not be passed to the model as pre-call expectation; use only to compute realized surprise/backtest.

consensus_by_topic.pre_call_expectation: Around R$3.5bn, with Bloomberg/LSEG close to R$3.46-3.495bn and public sell-side mostly around R$3.5-3.8bn except BTG's lower range.
High provisions were expected; exact magnitude had less source coverage. Genial estimated R$17.9bn for 1Q26 and broader commentary emphasized elevated credit cost.
Agro deterioration was already the core risk and was not, by itself, a new surprise.

consensus_by_topic.topic: Contamination beyond agro: individuals / cards / revolving credit
consensus_by_topic.pre_call_expectation: Some concern existed, but the degree to which non-agro credit would become central was less settled.
NII resilience was partly expected, but direct public estimates were limited; Genial estimated R$26.4bn.
Risk of revision was known, but magnitude and management framing were the real surprise variables.
Capital was a risk to monitor, but not as precisely quantified in public pre-call consensus as earnings and credit quality.
Market expected caution, but low visibility, lack of confidence in 2H26 normalization or openness to further revisions would be negative surprises.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: High provisions expected; risk of negative revision was known.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: Revision above R$60bn, management signaling pressure beyond agribusiness, or low visibility into 2H26 normalization.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: Formal prior guidance was R$22-26bn, but public pre-call views already questioned achievability after a weak 1Q26 start.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: Cutting the range so that the old floor becomes the new ceiling, especially if not paired with credible normalization path.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: Net income around R$3.5bn was expected by Bloomberg/LSEG and public sell-side previews.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: A deviation greater than roughly ±5% versus Bloomberg/LSEG, or evidence that earnings quality was materially weaker than headline net income suggested.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: Agro was already expected to be the main pressure point, with high NPLs, judicial recoveries and provisioning needs.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: A clear peak/normalization signal would be positive; evidence of further deterioration or weak recoveries would be negative.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: Some spillover risk was known, but agro remained the dominant expected pressure point before the call.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: Management explicitly highlighting material deterioration in individuals, credit card, revolving lines or SMEs as a second leg of credit pressure.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: Capital was a watch item given weaker profitability and elevated provisions, but not the most quantified public consensus topic.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: Capital discussion becoming central, signals of constrained payout, or management prioritizing capital preservation over shareholder remuneration.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: Sequential pressure was expected, but NII resilience was partly expected due to repricing/funding effects.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: NII materially above public estimate and strong enough to partly offset credit costs, or management raising NII guidance with credible drivers.

expected_vs_surprise_framework.pre_call_expectation: Cautious tone was expected; the market needed evidence on timing of normalization.
expected_vs_surprise_framework.what_would_be_surprising: Low confidence in 2H26 recovery, vague answers on peak provisions, or repeated emphasis that visibility remains limited.

public_proxy_consensus.method: mean/median of public datapoints: Bloomberg consensus, LSEG consensus, Genial, Itaú BBA, BTG midpoint, Bradesco BBI
public_proxy_consensus.interpretation: Lucro veio praticamente em linha com consenso formal Bloomberg/LSEG, mas abaixo de estimativas sell-side mais otimistas; dentro da faixa BTG.

narrative_consensus_before_call: O BB era esperado como o destaque negativo entre os grandes bancos no 1T26.
A pressão central era qualidade de ativos, especialmente agronegócio, mas já havia preocupação com PF e PJ.
Provisões/custo de crédito deveriam seguir elevados, com risco de revisão negativa do guidance de 2026.
NII/margem financeira seria pressionada sequencialmente por sazonalidade, menor tesouraria e custo de funding, mas ainda com resiliência na comparação anual.
A recuperação seria mais provável no 2S26, com baixa visibilidade no 1S26.

post_result_actuals_usage_note.strict_rule: post_result_actuals_for_backtesting is for realized surprise/backtesting only. It must not be treated as pre-call expectation or injected into prompts as prior_context.
allowed_uses: Compute surprise after parsing the call/result.
Evaluate whether model classifications match realized actuals.
Build unit tests for expected vs surprise logic.
disallowed_uses: Evidence that analysts expected a metric before the release.
Prompt context for a model that is supposed to infer surprise from the transcript alone.

surprise_interpretation_rules.guidance: Se lucro ajustado ficar dentro de ±3% do consenso formal Bloomberg/LSEG, classificar como 'in line'. Para BBAS3 1T26, o lucro de R$3,43 bi ficou em linha com Bloomberg/LSEG, apesar de fraco em termos absolutos.
Mesmo com lucro em linha, tratar custo de crédito, NPL, recuperações judiciais e revisão de guidance como potenciais surpresas negativas qualitativas.
NII acima de estimativas deve ser classificado como surpresa positiva operacional, mas não deve compensar automaticamente deterioração de crédito.
Revisão de lucro 2026 de R$22-26 bi para R$18-22 bi e custo de crédito de R$53-58 bi para R$65-70 bi deve ser classificada como principal surpresa negativa.

expected_analyst_questions: Qual é o pico esperado do custo de crédito e da inadimplência no agronegócio?
A revisão de guidance é suficiente ou ainda há risco de novo corte?
Quanto da pressão de crédito já está provisionada e quanto depende de recuperações no 2S26?
A deterioração começou a migrar de agro para PF/PJ? Quais linhas são mais sensíveis?
Como o BB Regulariza Agro e os efeitos residuais da MP 1.314 afetam capital, provisões e recuperação?
Qual o nível sustentável de ROE pós-normalização do agro?
O payout/dividendos continuará limitado pelo capital e pela rentabilidade deprimida?

avoid_overclaiming: Não dizer que o resultado de lucro foi grande surpresa negativa; foi fraco, mas em linha com consenso formal.
Não tratar cada fala negativa sobre agro como novidade se já estava no consenso pré-call.
Dar maior peso a guidance, custo de crédito, NPL early-stage/PF e recuperações judiciais como fontes de surpresa.

prompt_usage_guardrails: Never feed post_result_actuals_for_backtesting as if they were available before the call.

Sources with is_post_result_source=true can only contribute pre-call expectations when allowed_usage explicitly says they report a pre-result consensus figure, e.g., Bloomberg/LSEG consensus cited after the fact.
Do not classify 'agro pressure' alone as a surprise; it was known before the call.
Classify the 1Q26 adjusted net income as in-line versus formal consensus unless the model has a materially different consensus source.
Classify the 2026 guidance revision as the primary negative surprise, especially cost of credit and adjusted net income ranges.
When only public proxy consensus is available, cap confidence below a paid consensus dataset unless at least three independent pre-call sources agree.
